title: A paint tool throws your marquee away for good
goal: Draw a marquee, then pick up the brush or the rectangle, and the outline vanishes. Nothing brings it back: Command Z takes back your last edit to the picture instead, so an outline you spent time placing is lost to a single keystroke on the wrong tool. Either the tool should leave the marquee alone, or losing it should be one press to undo.
notes:
Found on 2026-09-08 while finishing undo-puts-back-a-selection-you-lost, and reproduced rather than read off the code.

Repro: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/undo-puts-back-the-marquee-walk.json

From its log.json, stage 11 (undo of a clear) then a tool switch to rectangle:
  11-undo-clear   region=405,300 200x100 layers=2 canUndo=True
  12-second-rect  region=none        layers=3 canUndo=True   <- after {"do":"tool","tool":"rectangle"}
  13-undo-picture region=none        layers=2 canUndo=True   <- undo took the rectangle back, outline still gone
  14-undo-selection region=400,300 200x100 layers=2          <- keeps stepping back past the run, never returns 405,300

Cause: EditorState.setTool does a raw `selection = nil` for a tool where `preservesSelectionRegion` is false (EditorState.swift:1561, Tools.swift:106). That write syncs to History but is never recorded as a step, deliberately, because restoring an outline while a brush is in hand shows ants the paint tool does not honour. So the fix is a UX call first: Photoshop keeps the selection across every tool change, which would make the whole question go away. Worth a decision card before code.
acceptance: Picking up a tool that cannot use a marquee either leaves the outline alone or records losing it, whichever the decision lands on
If it is recorded, one Command Z after picking that tool puts the outline back and the outline is legible on screen while that tool is in hand
If it is left alone, the outline is still there when you pick a marquee tool back up
Undo of a picture edit is unaffected either way

log.note: Reproduced in the app, smaller than the original report: blank document, marquee tool, drag a box, press R once. The outline is gone, the Selection X/Y/W/H section is gone from the panel, and Command Z brings back neither (it undoes the marquee-draw step itself, so nothing changes on screen). Walk: /tmp/marquee-lost-walk.json, shots under /tmp/photonz-playtest/marquee-lost-on-tool.

Adversarial review of the idea before building. (1) The existing behaviour is a deliberate choice with a written reason: dashed chrome that a paint tool will not honour reads as interactive. That reason is real, so this is not a plain bug fix, it is a reversal of a design call, and the user decides it. (2) The recorded-undo option (put the loss on the undo stack) lands you in a state the app otherwise says cannot exist, an outline up with a paint tool in hand, so it needs undo to hand the tool back too. That is two things per press. (3) The shortest version that delivers the value is simply not clearing the outline, which is what Photoshop does and what the app's own comment cites as the reason it preserves the outline inside the selection family. (4) Nothing decorative to cut here. To make the card decidable I built the keep-it option behind a throwaway patch, ran it, photographed it, and reverted; the working tree has no source changes.

Built the keep-it option temporarily and confirmed it behaves: rectangle tool in hand with the outline still up, drew a shape over it, the new layer got its blue outline and handles while the marquee kept its own black-and-white dashes. The two do not read as the same object. Panel swapped its Selection section for Position & Size rather than showing both. Source reverted afterwards.

Reproduced, then filed the decision "When you pick up a tool that cannot paint inside a marquee, what should happen to the outline you drew?" with four options and real before/after pictures of the app. Recommended: the outline stays up (Photoshop). Nothing shipped in code.
